description:
FILED s488a (Opus, 2026-09-17) by task #1834's member 2, while locating where
t/op/gv.t HANGS (#1651).  It is a Perl-semantics bug in its own right AND the
INSTRUMENT that makes every hang in the companion population unreadable.

PERL: `$| = 1` makes the next write hit the fd immediately, whatever the handle
is connected to.  PCL: nothing is written until the buffer fills or the program
exits normally, so a program killed while it runs has produced NO output at all.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL HEAD 46fb7645), stdout REDIRECTED TO A FILE:
    # af.pl
    $| = 1;
    print "a\n";
    for (1..40) { print "row $_\n" }
    my $t = time; 1 while time - $t < 30;
    print "b\n";

    $ perl af.pl > /tmp/p.out &   ; sleep 4; wc -c < /tmp/p.out   ->  273
    $ ./runpcl af.pl > /tmp/c.out & ; sleep 6; wc -c < /tmp/c.out ->    0

ALL THREE SPELLINGS of the flag fail the same way (each measured with its own
busy-loop program, bytes read mid-run):
    $| = 1; print "..."                              -> 0 bytes
    $| = 1; print STDOUT "..."                       -> 0 bytes
    select((select(STDOUT), $| = 1)[0]); print "..."  -> 0 bytes
And a 300-row (~9 KB) program writes 0 bytes mid-run, so this is not a small
buffer: nothing reaches the fd until exit.  SIGTERM does not flush either
(`timeout -k 5 8` leaves the file empty), so a killed run loses everything that
was still in the buffer.

WHERE (read, not probed): the machinery EXISTS and looks right --
`cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` has `*p-autoflush-handles*` (an `eq` hash, weak keys),
`%p-maybe-autoflush` (called from `%p-print-to` and `p-printf`), and the magic
cell for `|$\||` whose setter does
    (let ((s (%p-default-out)))
      (cond ((p-true-p new) (setf (gethash s *p-autoflush-handles*) t) ...)))
So the SETTER registers `(%p-default-out)` and the WRITE looks up the `fh` that
`%p-out-target` resolved.  The `eq` hash makes them the same entry only if both
sides answer the SAME OBJECT for STDOUT -- and the two paths reach it
differently (`*standard-output*` vs the stream pulled out of the STDOUT glob),
which is the first thing to measure: print the two objects at both sites and
compare with `eq`.  If they differ, the fix is to canonicalise the stream on
both sides (one helper), not to add a second table.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND $|:
  * #1651 (t/op/gv.t hangs) cannot be located from the timed-out run's kept
    `.out`: perl's t/test.pl sets `$| = 1` at its line 22 precisely so that a
    test file's TAP is on disk row by row.  Under PCL the kept output ends at
    whatever the last buffer flush happened to carry -- op/gv.t's keeps 91 rows
    / 5,711 bytes of TAP -- so "the last row is 93" bounds the hang from BELOW
    and up to one buffer (~4 KB ~ 60 rows) may be missing.  Any hang in the
    companion population is unreadable for the same reason.
  * A real program that reports progress to a log file shows nothing until it
    ends, and a program killed by a supervisor loses its whole log.

NOT FIXED HERE: a `cl/` change is a full-sweep + ir-conform bar and this batch
is an attribution pass (task #1834).  The fix is small if the diagnosis above
holds; the guard is a `Pl/t` row that runs a child with a redirected stdout and
reads the file WHILE the child still runs (a plain run cannot see the bug --
the buffer flushes at exit).


=== CORRECTED (s489, Fable, 2026-09-17) ===
The reproducer above was run under `./runpcl`.  Re-run at review with stdout
redirected to a file, the SAME program (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s489/probes/af.pl:
40 rows then a 12 s busy loop), bytes on disk after 5 s:
    perl                          273
    pcl af.pl > out               273   <- the runtime honours $|
    tools/pclperl-for-tests       273   <- the companion's child wrapper too
    ./runpcl af.pl > out            0   <- runpcl: my $out = `$sbcl_cmd 2>$errfile`; ... print $out;  at exit
With `$| = 1` REMOVED both perl and pcl show 0 mid-run; with a newline-less
`print` and the flag, both show 5.  So the runtime is right; the
`*p-autoflush-handles*` suspicion was never measured and is withdrawn.

WHAT IS TRUE FOR THE COMPANION (and keeps this task alive): tools/run-perl-suite.pl
runs each file in a shadow t/ whose `test.pl` is PCL's transpilable STUB
`perl-tests/t/test.pl` (runner ~line 673), and that stub has NO `$| = 1` --
perl's t/test.pl sets it at line 22.  So every companion file's TAP is
block-buffered: a TIMEOUT-killed file loses up to one buffer (~4 KB, ~60 rows),
and the C_ok/C_notok a TIMEOUT file reports is the rows that had FLUSHED, not
the rows that ran -- one root of #1851's flapping counts (uni/variables.t
1300/29413 vs 1300/24509 in the same run).

FIX SHAPE (two runner-side lines, no `cl/`):
  1. perl-tests/t/test.pl: add `$| = 1;` where perl's has it.  HARNESS change =>
     the harness bar: full sweep --jobs 4 + companion `--all --quick --jobs 2`
     (both populations reach it); TIMEOUT files' counts WILL move (upward, to
     the rows that ran) -- splice them ROW BY ROW with this task as the cause,
     never re-bless.
  2. runpcl: stream the program's stdout instead of capturing it (keep the
     stderr filter on the errfile).
GUARD: a tools/t row that a `$| = 1` program run through pclperl-for-tests /
runpcl has its first line on disk before it exits.


=== DONE (s473t6b, Opus, 2026-09-17) â commit c4f493ff ===

Both runner-side lines shipped, and a THIRD that the s489 re-scope could not
have known about because it is not a runner at all.

1. `perl-tests/t/test.pl` â `$| = 1;` where perl's t/test.pl has it (its line
   22), with the reason in the comment.

2. THE STUB LINE ALONE CHANGES NOTHING, and that is the finding.  Measured
   before writing it: a 41-row file whose 41st row is behind a 45 s busy loop,
   run through the companion's own child command (a fresh core = runtime +
   testlib, `p-load-with-recovery`, cwd = a shadow t/), stdout to a file, bytes
   read mid-run â
       base                     0 bytes mid-run / 603 at exit
       stub `$| = 1` only       0 / 603        <- unchanged
       stub + the fix below   588 / 603        <- perl's own 588 / 603
   Because `%tap-out` â the ONE writer every TAP line goes through
   (cl/pcl-test.lisp) â calls `%p-out-string`, a bare `write-string`, and never
   consulted `*p-autoflush-handles*`.  So the second half is one line in that
   writer, `(%p-maybe-autoflush *standard-output*)`, routed through the
   EXISTING autoflush mechanism rather than an unconditional force-output:
   `%tap-out` IS the equivalent of the `print` perl's harness uses, so it obeys
   the same flag and nothing else.  With $| off the cost is one fixnum read of
   an empty hash table.  The NEGATIVE was probed too: with `$| = 0` in the test
   file both perl and PCL write 0 bytes mid-run and 603 at exit.

3. `runpcl` â `system("$sbcl_cmd 2>$errfile")` instead of
   `my $out = \`...\`` plus a `print $out` at exit, so the child owns fd 1 and
   WHEN a byte appears is the program's business.  #1850's own af.pl at 12 s:
   perl 273, runpcl 0 -> 273, `pcl` 273; 275 at exit for all three.

   ONE CONSEQUENCE, measured and documented in runpcl: under
   `runpcl prog 2>&1` the streams now arrive stdout-then-stderr where the
   capture gave stderr-then-stdout.  Neither order was the program's â the old
   one came from the PARENT's buffering (captured stdout sat in a
   block-buffered pipe while `print STDERR` went straight out), which happened
   to match `perl prog 2>&1` only because perl's stdout is block-buffered to a
   pipe too.  Matching perl in general would mean filtering stderr
   INCREMENTALLY (the note strip is a whole-text look-ahead), which buys
   ordering in a capture and costs the one thing that matters in a program.
   All six Pl/t files that capture `./runpcl â¦ 2>&1` pass (185 rows), and the
   exit status and `PCL_SHOW_SBCL` line are identical to the base.

GUARD: `tools/t/runpcl-streams.t` 8 -> 15 rows.  A plain run cannot see this
bug (the buffer flushes at exit either way), so the rows use a RACE the program
itself decides â first line, busy window, MARKER file, busy window, last line â
and poll for whichever appears first.  TWO windows, not one: with a single
window the marker write, the last print and the exit flush all landed inside
one 50 ms tick, so the buffered case read `stdout` too and the row could not
fail.  Inverse-verified on a f26282db extraction: rows 9 (runpcl), 13 (TAP) and
15 (the stub line) FAIL there; row 11 (pclperl-for-tests) passes on both, which
is the reference this task named.

THE HARNESS BAR:
  * full sweep `--jobs 4`: GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, TOTAL passing
    18686 = baseline, drops 5 = census, CAUSES 480 of 480.  So the perl-tests
    population does not move: its own runner loads the same stub, and the rows
    that were being lost were only ever lost in a file the runner KILLED, which
    the sweep's 90 s + retry does not do to these files.
  * companion `--all --quick --jobs 2`, one run: see the round's record.

THE COMPANION BAR, and what it actually measured (s473t6b, resumed 2026-09-18).
The `--all --quick --jobs 2` run of 22:49-23:32 was left as an ORPHAN and the
TREE CHANGED UNDER IT (two later commits landed at 23:10 and 23:20, and every
spawn re-keys its core on the runtime's content hash), so it is read for LEADS
only.  Every file it flagged was re-measured `--jobs 1` on the finished tree AND
on a `git archive f26282db` extraction:

  io/crlf_through.t   942/0 OK on both   (the orphan's "-318 passing" was its own
  io/through.t        942/0 OK on both    contamination, not a mover)
  io/pvbm.t           23/5 = the blessed value (the known flapper)
  op/gv.t             TIMEOUT (#1651) -- a load-dependent count, never a mover
  re/charset.t        5224/328 = the blessed value; its 506 "FIXED ROW"s are the
                      500-row log cap, which makes that file's ROW baseline partial
  op/tiehandle.t      base 12/32 -> 11/32   <- REAL, and this task's
  uni/stash.t         base 44/6  -> 43/6    <- REAL, and this task's

THE TWO REAL ONES ARE ONE MECHANISM, and it is the point of the change: with the
TAP on disk ROW BY ROW, a NON-TAP write that ends WITHOUT A NEWLINE now glues to
the next TAP row (`sometextok 22`) instead of landing elsewhere in the old block
buffer's flush order, and that row stops being PARSEABLE.  perl with `$| = 1`
glues the same way -- it is what unbuffered output MEANS.  Both files only
produce such a write because something upstream already diverges: op/tiehandle.t
prints "sometext" on the REAL handle because `tie *$fh` is DROPPED (#155), and
uni/stash.t ends a `p-load-with-recovery` diagnostic without a newline.  Proved
by byte-diffing the two `.out` files from `PCL_SUITE_KEEP` runs of both trees:
the glue is the ONLY difference.  Both verdicts spliced into
baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv with that cause, and the two rows carry it in
baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv.

The full sweep was re-run on the finished tree (member 0 + two runtime fixes):
GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed / 0 LOST, TOTAL passing 18686 (+0), drops 5 = census.


=== REVIEW ADDENDUM (Fable, s490, main 8d699b91) ===
The batch's own `--all --quick` ran as an orphan while two commits landed under it, and the brief's "TIMEOUT files' counts spliced with #1850" was not done.  Fable re-ran `--all --quick --jobs 2` on the FINAL tree (log ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s490/review/t6b-companion.log) and spliced: snapshot op/gv.t TIMEOUT 67/24 -> 90/95, uni/gv.t 0/0 -> 75/84, re/regexp_qr_embed_thr.t NOTAP 202/1656 -> 242/1787, uni/variables.t C_ok 1248 -> 1300 (parallel and serial agreeing on each) -- a file the runner kills now keeps every row that RAN; and six fail rows LEFT by per-file bless (io/open.t rows 41 + 89 "not inherited across exec" and their two *extra* twins -- an exec'd child's rows now land in ORDER, the ordering half of #1707; the *summary* rows of io/crlf.t and uni/fold.t).  Residue filed: #1849 (a RATE-LIMITED timeout file's C_notok is load-dependent now).
subject: RE-SCOPED s489 (Fable review of s488a): the RUNTIME honours `$|` -- `pcl FILE > out` and `tools/pclperl-for-tests` write 273 bytes mid-run like perl; what hides it is (1) `runpcl`, which captures the program's stdout with BACKTICKS and prints it at exit, and (2) the companion HARNESS STUB `perl-tests/t/test.pl`, which lacks perl test.pl's line-22 `$| = 1` -- so a TIMEOUT-killed companion file still loses up to one buffer of TAP and its counts are the rows that FLUSHED (a root of #1851).  Fix = the stub line + runpcl streaming, HARNESS bar (full sweep + companion --all --quick)
